summary: No blocking correctness or architecture defect was found in the phase diff. Required copy, price, removed-claim, caller, and test checks pass. Four visual concerns remain for the planned browser-review role; none violates an explicit functional acceptance criterion by itself.
nonblocking_findings: [Medium] Review A: apps/www-reading-advantage/public/images/features/primary-lesson-step05.webp (spec.md:117; plan.md:51,69) | The provided screenshot shows a Student preview / Exit preview banner. Spec.md:117 names the source as the student-preview screen and does not require its removal, while plan.md:51 and :69 broadly ask the image/look reviewers to reject banners. Treat this as a planned visual review question, not a confirmed FR-3 defect; check the source crop against the intended page before acceptance.

[Low] Review A: apps/www-reading-advantage/src/components/features/program-card.tsx:49-55 (spec.md:107; plan.md:69) | The no-photo cards render a large blank panel and a white square. D7 says to show no picture when no fitting asset exists; this has no broken-image violation, but it may look like an unfinished image placeholder. The browser reviewer should decide whether the empty treatment meets the specified text-first layout.

[Low] Review A: apps/www-reading-advantage/src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:122-129 (source spec §4 S4, lines 252-253) | The three included-benefit tiles use text-sm. The copy and count match the source, and the spec sets no font-size minimum; the reported tiny appearance is a readability concern for the browser reviewer, not a proven contract failure.

[Low] Review A: apps/www-reading-advantage/src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/features/page.tsx:185-193 (source spec §3 S3, lines 146-149; spec.md:107) | The Mastery Advantage panel uses three plain color bars rather than an identifiable workbook-and-knowledge-map illustration. D7 also directs text-first rendering when no suitable image exists, so this is a visual-fit question for the browser reviewer, not a confirmed functional failure.
